(1) black spruce families differ in shoot water potential, osmotic potential at saturation, and modulus of elasticity; (2) the magnitude of these genetic differences are similar on a dry and wet site; and (3) the magnitude of differences in shoot water potential between families is greatest on the dry site and during dry growing season conditions.

black spruce trees from a family that displayed a positive growth response to a wet environment had higher shoot water potentials and lower osmotic potentials than a family displaying a negative growth response to a dry environment.
